kind: Independent root mathematical review of reconstructed analytical source
review_method: Direct line-by-line mathematical reasoning over the actual source; no numerical experiment or automated theorem prover was run.

checks.finding: Subtraction uses the same terminal cost and the updated action applied to the incumbent continuation.
rho(v)-rho(v-h) is an infimum of E_q h plus the nonnegative centered penalty; the sign is correct.
Infimum of centered penalties is zero by approximate maximizers of the finite risk value.
0<=k_lower<=k implies normalization, operator order, monotonicity, cash invariance and norm nonexpansiveness.
b_star>=b>=0 and beta>=0 prove 0<=H_lower<=H<=D by backward induction.
A lower subsolution is below the minimizing value; one feasible dual kernel/flow is an upper bound and cannot certify gain.
Stage b has B_t coefficient and nonnegative penalty has B_(t+1); flow cancellation does not divide by beta and covers zero discount.
A finite subset of a risk set raises its infimum and is explicitly disallowed as an unjustified lower certificate.
Both policy maps and gain maps preserve the full complete B_b domain and are beta contractions for beta<1.
Iteration of all three maps from zero proves nonnegativity and ordering; arbitrary bounded nonnegative subsolutions converge upwards to the conservative fixed point.
Strong convexity/smoothness and future error are separately assumed for the same incumbent one-step objective at every state; the two-date allowance is not reused without proof.
No optimal policy-iteration convergence, risk query complexity, neural exclusivity or longer-horizon numerical claim is inferred.
